summary: Quintet and Enix's action/simulation series, covering the original ActRaiser, the action-focused sequel, and Square Enix's modern remake Actraiser Renaissance.

entries.title: ActRaiser

emulation.emulator: bsnes, MiSTer SNES core, or original hardware
emulation.notes: Use high-accuracy SNES emulation for the original game.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original SNES presentation with accurate emulation and modern capture.

primary.why: For the original game, the SNES version is the complete source release; the 2004 mobile version removed the town-building portions and only covered the first three action stages, while Wii Virtual Console is an older emulated route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original SNES/Super Famicom release on hardware, MiSTer, or a high-accuracy emulator such as bsnes using an owned copy. Treat Actraiser Renaissance as a separate remake entry.

all_releases.reason: primary: complete original version and the baseline for comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Limited mobile adaptation containing only the first three side-scrolling levels and omitting town-building portions.

all_releases.reason: skip: convenient historical digital route, but no longer the main practical recommendation.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The mobile version is lower-completeness because it omits the simulation portions; Renaissance is a separate remake with altered flow and extra content rather than the original version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Actraiser Renaissance is a distinct remake with extra commands, tower-defense segments, and a post-game stage, so it is cataloged separately.

entries.title: ActRaiser 2

emulation.emulator: bsnes, MiSTer SNES core, or original hardware
emulation.notes: Use high-accuracy SNES emulation for clean capture.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original SNES presentation with accurate emulation and modern capture.

primary.why: ActRaiser 2 was released for the SNES/Super Famicom and has no sourced modern remaster or port; the original release is the complete version.
primary.how_to_play: Play on SNES hardware, MiSTer, or a high-accuracy emulator such as bsnes using an owned copy.

all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced release and therefore the complete version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced alternate release or exclusive-content split.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced modern remaster or re-release.

entries.title: Actraiser Renaissance

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the PC version.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native modern remake presentation on PC.

primary.why: Actraiser Renaissance is a remake released for PC, PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch, iOS, and Android; PC/Steam is the highest-fidelity and most capture-friendly version, and the remake adds altered action controls, tower-defense segments, and a post-game stage.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam/Windows version for the cleanest capture and settings. Console or mobile versions are acceptable if preferred, but they do not add exclusive content.

all_releases.fidelity: Steam/Windows release of the modern remake.
all_releases.reason: primary: best capture and display-control route for the remake.
skip: same core remake content, less flexible for capture than PC.
skip: same core remake content, less flexible for capture than PC.
skip: portable route, but not the best capture/fidelity option.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced content split across the remake platforms; PC is preferred for fidelity and capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a remake that changes the original flow with new action inputs, tower-defense segments, and a post-game stage; keep it separate from the SNES original.
